Let me try with a User-Agent header and X-Browser-Fingerprint header properly. Actually, the flow is: signin creates session, then user_device_log runs. Let me retry with the X-Browser-Fingerprint header on the signin request.

Actually, I initially used X-Zammad-User-Fingerprint. The correct header is X-Browser-Fingerprint. But this check only happens when session[:user_device_updated_at] is nil. Let me just provide the header.

action.command:
cd /workspace
rm -f /tmp/cookies.txt
curl -s -c /tmp/cookies.txt --max-time 30 http://127.0.0.1:3000/ -o /dev/null
CSRF=$(curl -s -b /tmp/cookies.txt -c /tmp/cookies.txt --max-time 30 http://127.0.0.1:3000/ | grep -oE 'csrf-token" content="[^"]*"' | head -1 | sed 's/.*content="//;s/"//')
curl -s -b /tmp/cookies.txt -c /tmp/cookies.txt --max-time 30 -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/v1/signin \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-CSRF-Token: $CSRF" \
  -H "X-Browser-Fingerprint: 1234567890abcdef" \
  -H "User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0 (X11; Linux x86_64) AppleWebKit/537.36" \
  -d '{"username":"admin@example.com","password":"test"}' -w "\nHTTP %{http_code}\n" | tail -15
